entries.name: CDP-Linked Local Brokers
entries.summary: Traditional Singapore brokerages that settle SGX trades straight into your own name at the Central Depository (CDP), so you hold shares directly rather than through the broker.
entries.analogy: Like registering a car in your own name at the land transport authority, instead of leasing it under the dealer's name.
pros: Shares are registered in your own name at CDP — dividends and voting rights (e.g. AGM invites) come directly to you
Long-established players regulated by MAS, with decades of track record
Access to IPOs, rights issues and corporate actions handled directly via CDP
Full range of order types and, for many, access to remisier/full-service support
cons: Commissions for cash accounts are typically higher than app-based custodian brokers
Opening a CDP account is an extra step compared to custodian brokers
Platforms can feel dated compared to newer mobile-first apps
Custody/settlement fees may apply if you trade infrequently
entries.bestFor: Investors who want SGX shares registered in their own name and don't mind a slightly higher cost for that.
entries.eligibility: 18 years or older with a CDP Securities account; a Singapore bank account is generally required for CDP's direct crediting service.

entries.name: Custodian / App-Based Brokers
entries.summary: Mobile-first brokers that hold your shares in a custodian (trust) structure rather than in your own CDP name, usually with lower fees and faster account opening.
entries.analogy: Like keeping valuables in a bank's safe deposit box under the bank's custodial arrangement — convenient and low-cost, just not titled directly to you at the registry.
pros: Often the lowest commissions and platform fees among SG-accessible brokers
Fast, fully digital account opening — usually minutes, not days
Fractional share investing available on some platforms for US stocks
Slick mobile apps with built-in charting, news and community features
cons: Shares are held in the broker's custodian/trust structure, not your own CDP name
Corporate action handling (rights issues, AGM votes) may be less direct than CDP-linked
Newer entrants have a shorter regulatory track record than the established local brokers
Promotional zero-commission periods often revert to standard fees after a set time
entries.bestFor: Cost-conscious, mobile-first investors comfortable with a custodian holding structure.
entries.eligibility: 18 years or older; account opening usually via Singpass MyInfo or passport/ID upload.

entries.name: International Brokers
entries.summary: Large global brokers offering access to dozens of exchanges worldwide from a single account, popular with investors who trade beyond SG/US/HK or want institutional-grade tools.
entries.analogy: Like a universal travel adapter — one account plugs you into markets all over the world.
pros: Access to a very wide range of global exchanges and instruments from one account
Generally very competitive commissions, especially for active or larger traders
Sophisticated trading tools, order types and research
Strong regulatory pedigree with operations across many jurisdictions
cons: Interfaces can be overwhelming for a first-time investor
Inactivity or account-level fees may apply depending on the tier
Customer support is less localised than a Singapore-based broker
Currency conversion and multi-currency account management add a layer of complexity
entries.bestFor: Investors who want global market access and are comfortable with a more complex platform.
entries.eligibility: 18 years or older; account opening via online application with identity verification.

entries.name: Bank-Integrated Brokers
entries.summary: Brokerage accounts run by or tightly integrated with your everyday bank (DBS, OCBC, UOB), so you can view holdings and trade within the same banking app you already use.
entries.analogy: Like having a savings account and a trading account under the same roof, viewable on one login.
pros: Single login to view banking, savings and investments together
Trusted, familiar brand if you already bank with them
Funding and withdrawals are usually instant between your bank and trading accounts
Branch support available if you prefer speaking to someone in person
cons: Commissions can be higher than dedicated app-based custodian brokers
Product range may nudge you toward the bank's own funds and structured products
Trading platform is often less feature-rich than specialist brokers
Account opening may require an existing deposit account with the bank
entries.bestFor: Existing bank customers who value convenience and a single view of banking plus investments.
entries.eligibility: Typically requires an active deposit/internet banking account with the bank.

entries.name: Full-Service / Remisier Brokers
entries.summary: A human remisier or dealer manages your trades and gives market commentary, typically through one of the established local brokerages, for a higher commission than self-directed online trading.
entries.analogy: Like using a travel agent instead of booking flights yourself — more personal service, at a higher cost.
pros: A dedicated remisier/dealer to call for trade execution and market updates
Useful for investors less comfortable navigating an online platform themselves
Can provide access to IPO allocations and research the remisier curates
Offered as an option by most established CDP-linked brokers, so due diligence overlaps
cons: Commissions are meaningfully higher than self-directed online trading
Quality and incentives vary a lot by individual remisier
Slower execution than placing your own online order
Less transparency into why a particular trade is recommended unless you ask
entries.bestFor: Investors who want a personal relationship and are willing to pay more for guided execution.
entries.eligibility: 18 years or older with a CDP Securities account; opened through the remisier's brokerage firm.

entries.name: Fund Platforms
entries.summary: Broker-adjacent platforms specialised in unit trusts and funds across many fund houses, often bundled with advisory or robo-style portfolio options on the same account.
entries.analogy: Like a fund supermarket where every aisle is a different fund manager, all checked out at one till.
pros: Very wide fund shelf across many fund houses in one account
Often lower sales charges than buying the same fund via a bank branch
Some platforms combine self-directed fund buying with advisory portfolios
Can consolidate cash, SRS and sometimes CPF fund holdings in one place
cons: Platform fees apply even where sales charges are discounted or waived
Primarily funds — not the venue for buying individual stocks directly
Choice overload without a clear plan for what to buy
Some products require extra risk acknowledgements before purchase
entries.bestFor: Investors who want broad fund selection and lower sales charges than a bank branch.
entries.eligibility: 18 years or older; account opening via Singpass MyInfo or manual verification.

entries.name: MAS-Licensed Crypto Exchanges
entries.summary: Platforms licensed by MAS as Major Payment Institutions to offer Digital Payment Token (DPT) services, letting you buy, sell and hold cryptocurrencies. Crypto is highly volatile and not suitable for most beginner portfolios.
entries.analogy: Like a currency exchange counter for a currency that can swing wildly in value overnight — the counter being licensed doesn't make the currency itself safe.
pros: MAS licensing means the exchange itself meets baseline anti-money-laundering and operational standards
24/7 market access and near-instant transfers between exchanges/wallets
Wide range of digital assets available compared to traditional brokers
Licensing is checkable directly on the MAS Financial Institutions Directory
cons: Extreme price volatility — cryptocurrency values can fall sharply and rapidly
MAS licensing regulates the exchange's conduct, not the safety of the underlying asset — you can still lose most or all of your money
Not covered by SDIC deposit insurance or the same investor protections as securities
Common target for scams — always transact only through the exchange's own licensed app or site
entries.bestFor: Only experienced investors who understand and accept the risk of losing their entire investment; not a starting point for beginners.
entries.eligibility: 18 years or older; identity verification required. Always confirm current licensing status on the MAS Financial Institutions Directory before transacting, as licences and entities can change.
